title: From A Double Life Sentence to MAGA Influencer Fame
content:
A year ago I quit my job to go full time independent. It’s clearer than ever that we need a robust independent media ecosystem to hold power to account, and the only reason I’m able to do the work I do (not just this newsletter, but my bi-weekly videos, my Free Speech Friday series educating people on civil liberties, my podcast, my social media content, my tech policy and civil rights advocacy work, and so much more)— is because of those of you who pay to support this newsletter.

Since the vast majority of my paid subscribers signed up right after I went independent, these next couple months are extremely make it or break it. I hope that if you like my work, you’ll renew your subscription or purchase a paid one and give me the opportunity to remain independent for another year. 🙏

(If you prefer not to subscribe on Substack btw, I’m also now on Patreon).

Subscribe now

Nearly a decade ago, Ross Ulbricht, the founder of the Silk Road dark web marketplace was sentenced to a double life sentence in prison. Now, he’s out and has become a powerful influencer and political figure in the MAGA movement.

Ryan Mac at the New York Times has been covering Ulbricht for over a decade. He joined me to dive deep into Ulbrict’s’ past, how the Silk Road transformed the web, and how this crazy alliance between bitcoin billionaires, libertarians, and MAGA die-hards has skyrocketed Ulbricht to fame and set him up for a major role in politics.

User Mag is a 100% reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, become a free or paid subscriber.

User Mag news rundown

  • Cory Doctorow’s fantastic new book Enshittification, is finally out!

  • Jimmy Fallon wants to turn Wordle into a TV show.

  • Brands that fear for their survival unless they can connect with young people are fueling a boom in the business of “Gen Z translation.”

  • Time spent on social media peaked in 2022 and has since gone into steady decline.

  • JD Vance is back on TikTok.

  • The New Museum is hosting a vibe coding battle.

  • An LA-based designer made an app called Endless Summer “for when burnout hits and you need to manifest the soft life you deserve,” that allows you to scroll a feed of fake AI generated vacation photos with you in them.

  • Sora has bumped Google’s Gemini and ChatGPT from the top of the App Store.

  • Landlords are using a service that logs into a potential renter’s employer systems and scrapes their paystubs and other information en masse.

  • TrueAnon got the NYT treatment.

  • The millennial women of CougarTok open up about their 20-something boyfriends.

  • The 6-7 kid launched a pump and dump meme coin.

  • Everything that happened on Gavin Newsom’s appearance on Fortnite Friday last week.

  • Even Swifties are admitting that Taylor’s new album isn’t that great.

  • People are opening up about their “party gap” relationships, where one person wants to go out way more than the other.

  • 70% of Americans think the economy is on the ‘wrong track’.

  • Once a loyal foot soldier for Trump, Marjorie Taylor Greene is increasingly bucking her party.

  • Your therapist’s notes could become fodder for AI.

  • Cosmic Orange iPhones are turning pink.

  • Thirty Bob Ross paintings are being put up for auction to support public TV stations after federal funding cuts.

  • MrBeast says the rapid advance of generative AI is “scary” for the “millions of creators currently making content for a living”.

  • Gen Z women are the most liberal group in the country.

  • Israel is planning to run a massive propaganda campaign through ChatGPT.

  • Influencers who boosted Trump last year including Theo Von, Joe Rogan, and Andrew Schulz are starting to distance themselves.

  • Adin Ross reveals he regrets going the political route last year, saying too many people associate him with politics now.

  • Comedian turned right wing influencer Russell Brand, facing rape and assault charges in the UK, says he’s taking a step back and ending his career as a MAGA influencer.

  • The share of Americans who say college education is ‘very important’ has fallen from 75% in 2010 down to 35% in 2025 according to Gallup research.

  • Facemash, a website allowing users to rank the attractiveness of Harvard students, briefly returned to campus on Sunday, nearly 22 years after Mark Zuckerberg created the original version.

  • MAGA influencer Jack Posobiec appears to have committed voter fraud.

  • Apple removed the ICEBlock app, which helped user’s identify nearby ICE activity, after attacks from the Trump administration

  • Robin Williams’ daughter asks people to stop creating and sending her AI videos of her late father.

  • An analysis of 1,100 TikTok users’ watch histories across six months in 2024 shows just how effective TikTok is at getting even its heaviest users to watch more.
